title: Innovation Quant Developer Intern (DeFi/Corporate Development) - London
descriptionHtml:
Innovation Quant Developer: Intern - DeFi/Corporate Development

Since 2017, Keyrock has been a change-maker in digital assets. We're a global, remote-first team of 200+ people across 40+ nationalities, with hubs in Brussels, London, Paris and New York.

 

We provide liquidity across 80+ centralized and decentralized exchanges - a position cemented by our Series C, led by SC Ventures. Today we run a full spectrum of capital markets businesses across centralized and on-chain venues: market making, high-frequency trading, options, OTC, DeFi trading desks, advisory, and asset management.

 

We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement.

We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it.

About the Internship Program

Our internship programme gives early-career talent the opportunity to build practical skills, contribute to meaningful projects and learn alongside experienced colleagues in digital finance.

Typically lasting six months and based in our Brussels office (London possible), each internship includes hands-on experience, clear learning goals and dedicated guidance and regular feedback. We look for curiosity, relevant foundational skills, deep, active interest and passion for digital assets and the potential to grow exponentially with us - you don’t need to arrive with all the answers. Where performance, business needs and available opportunities align, an internship may lead to a permanent role, though this is not guaranteed.

We are looking for 3-4 high-caliber Quantitative Analyst Interns to sit within our Linear Market Making, DeFi trading , Credit/curation and Corporate Development desks/teams (see other openings on our career page for details).

Application deadline: 30 November 2026
Start date: 1 March 2027

Selection process:

  • Interview with Talent Acquisition representative

  • Interview with Hiring Manager

  • Recruitment Challenge

  

The role

About Corporate Development
In our Corporate Development team, we identify, evaluate, prototype, and build strategic innovations across digital asset markets and Web3 ecosystems. Operating at the intersection of quantitative analysis, technology due diligence, and venture/strategic growth, the Corp Dev team works on evaluating emerging crypto primitives, building data-driven systems to track market trends, and assessing the technical viability of potential deals, partnerships, and new business lines. As an Innovation Quant Developer Intern, you will work directly with quant developers and Corp Dev strategists to prototype new technologies, conduct technical due diligence, and support strategic growth initiatives.

Key Responsibilities of an Innovation Quant Developer Intern in this unit

  • Web3 Primitive & Technology Evaluation: Assist in evaluating new Web3.0 primitives, DeFi protocols, and emerging blockchain infrastructure, analyzing engineering requirements to align with Corporate Development growth goals.

  • Technical Due Diligence & Strategic Analysis: Support technical and quantitative due diligence on potential strategic deals, venture investments, and ecosystem partnerships to evaluate architectural viability and strategic fit.

  • Prototyping & System Integration: Help build, test, and maintain prototype systems, analytics tools, and internal proof-of-concepts, collaborating across divisions to ensure compatibility with Keyrock's broader trading and tech stack.

  • Market Intelligence & Data Analytics: Use Python, SQL, and data analytics to track emerging technologies, monitor market trends, and deliver actionable data-driven insights for strategic growth opportunities.

Who You Are/Key Requirements

  • Technical & Quantitative Foundation: Graduating student or recent graduate in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Quantitative Finance, or a related technical field with a solid code-first foundation in Python and SQL (with Git proficiency).

  • Web3 & Digital Asset Passion: Strong understanding of and active, deep interest in Web3.0, digital assets, blockchain primitives, and capital markets.

  • Analytical & Prototyping Mindset: Ability to analyze technical documentation, work with data/on-chain telemetry, evaluate emerging technologies, and build quantitative models or prototype tools.

  • Drive & Ownership: Self-starter with strong communication skills, curiosity to learn rapidly, and an owner mentality to contribute directly to strategic projects.

  • Nice-to-Haves: Hands-on experience prototyping smart contracts or Web3 tools, familiarity with Rust, Solidity, EVM event logs, or previous internship/project experience in crypto or quantitative finance.

Our offer

  • A 6 month paid internship at world-renowned digital assets company with accommodation provided for entirety or part of it

  • The opportunity to learn about digital assets and blockchain from a 30,000 ft view of the entire ecosystem

  • Working from one of Brussels newest, nicest and most advanced office spaces

  • A global, collaborative and tech-driven environment.

  • Autonomy & Impact - our flat structure means you can contribute your ideas from day one and help shape the foundation that will power Keyrock’s future business.

  • Culture of Excellence - we value nimbleness, drive for success, owner mentality and collaboration.

  • Opportunity to leave your mark and start your career in one of the most reputable companies in the digital assets world

  • We are envisioning for the internship to be based pre-dominantly in Brussels. It is possible for a selected candidate to be based in London, UK, provided at least 1-2 months onboarding period would be spent in Brussels together with the rest of the interns cohort.

 

Our recruitment philosophy

We value self-awareness and powerful communication skills in our recruitment process. We seek fiercely passionate people who understand themselves and their career goals. We're after those with the right skills and a conscious choice to join our field. The perfect fit? A crypto enthusiast who’s driven, collaborative, acts with ownership and delivers solid, scalable outcomes.

As an employer we are committed to building a positive and collaborative work environment. We welcome employees of all backgrounds, and hire, reward and promote entirely based on merit and performance.

Due to the nature of our business and external requirements, we perform background checks on all potential employees, passing which is a prerequisite to join Keyrock.

title: Innovative Project Planner (Data Centres / Buildings / High-tech / Infrastructure) - UK (Hybrid)
descriptionHtml:
Are you a bit tired of the standard, old-fashioned way of doing things in the construction industry? Do you get deep satisfaction from making things run more efficiently using a good dose of common sense and maybe a bit of technology? Have you always cared about the importance of proper planning and the connection between the schedule and the real, day-to-day delivery of the job? Have you ever wanted to work a bit more flexibly but still be hands-on in construction and improving the industry? Sounds like a dream. Well, it isn’t. It’s quite real! Read on. ____________________________________________________________ We are Laminar Projects! If you’ve already heard about us, you’re probably reading this because you’re tired of the typical, chaotic ways of doing things in construction. But in case you haven’t, we’re a high-end project management consultancy and tech developer with a focus on upgrading the way construction projects are delivered. Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Check out our short film about it.) We bring transparency and control to projects through a pragmatic mix of the latest tech, our own processes, and a big dose of common sense. We then take our deep understanding of these projects and we invest heavily into developing the digital solutions that anyone can use to deliver their projects better. (Check out Shape, our construction management tech, to see what we’re doing.) The core of all this is our true secret sauce: our people. We only recruit the very best, both in capability and personality. We’re deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that’s optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People who join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined. (Read more about our vision and missions.) This approach has allowed us to grow from just two people in 2017 to over 220 today. We have a stable, repeat client base across infrastructure and complex building projects in the UK and internationally, and we’re still growing fast. Joining us isn’t just some “job”. It’s a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life. There are many diverse and interesting challenges available. It’s up to you to guide yourself into whichever areas you’re most interested – we’ll enable it. (Get to know us better by watching a few more of our videos.) Core values for a good life A life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships and challenging yourself to create a positive impact, so our values reflect the four levels of relationships that each of us has: - Grow yourself – your relationship with yourself - Care about people – your relationship with others around you - Execute to greatness – your relationship with your team - Build civilisation – your relationship with humanity and the world We enshrined our values in our vision: We exist so that everyone in our team can flourish in a high-impact community that: - Connects us with meaningful relationships - Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans - Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures By first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world. And enable the achievement of our vision through our two missions: - To fully digitalise the construction of human civilisation - To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society ____________________________________________________________ The Role Purpose of the role You’ll be enhancing the delivery of the most complex and interesting projects in the world through the power of project planning to the very highest standards. You’ll devise strategies and tactics to improve the way the project is delivered. You’ll translate this knowledge into a logic-linked plan and analyse it using planning software. Then you’ll use the plan to help the teams understand what to prioritise. Your team This role is part of our Project Management Consultancy team which focuses on: - Understanding what the real problems of projects are - Implementing the best solutions to those problems - Developing scalable best practices, tools and technology More specifically, you’ll be part of our Project Planning Team, who are industry leaders in the planning of complex construction projects. Your initial leader will be one of our planning discipline directors. Your top three objectives 1. To make construction projects deliver to near perfection 2. To create scalable and repeatable solutions to common problems 3. To develop yourself and everyone around you Your top five responsibilities 1. Own the plan: Own the project plan for one or more projects and ensure that the project is working to it effectively. Ensure delays are mitigated and managed commercially 2. Own the outcome: You're responsible for putting in your best effort to ensure the project team’s understanding and focus on the plan – no matter how stubborn they are 3. Report and inform: Provide simple, actionable reports to stakeholders at all levels that help them deliver their part of the project more efficiently and effectively 4. Make scalable solutions: Develop scalable and repeatable best practices and tools in collaboration with the team so that long-term impact is achieved 5. Develop everyone: Maximise the development of your team personally and professionally and educate our clients to improve as well You must have: - A construction engineering background: You have at least 2+ years of experience on construction projects, experience in project planning both software and principles, as well as decent Excel skills, and a strong interest in data - Communication skills: You’re proficient in written and verbal English and have the charisma and influence to get construction people to do new things and take the best approach - Leadership capabilities: You lead yourself proactively and lead others by asking the right questions and challenging them - Impact: You have a track record of making projects and organisations better beyond just doing the basics – implementing scalable, repeatable solutions that had a significant positive impact Laminar isn’t the place for you if any of the following is true: - You want an easy, chilled-out role without much challenge - You like to be the smartest person in the room - You don’t like continuously receiving honest candid feedback - You prefer to do your own thing rather than work with a team ____________________________________________________________ Frequently Asked Questions What kinds of projects would I be working on? It’s common for people to be exposed to several projects in their first year with us. You’ll work on some of the most complex and interesting environments in the world. We’ve delivered over 100 data centres internationally, many of them fast-tracked and multi-package. Our teams have supported flagship infrastructure programmes like HS2 through integrated planning and digital delivery, contributed to over $30bn in power generation and transmission projects, and played a key role in the development of high-containment labs and R&D campuses for some of the world’s most advanced industrial and life sciences clients. You might find yourself working in sectors such as data centres, infrastructure (including defense, rail, and highways), high tech (such as advanced manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and semiconductors), or complex building projects. These aren’t hands-off assignments. They’re dynamic, hands-on environments designed for people who want to be challenged. We bring back the lessons from every project to help our team grow and deliver the highest levels of value. (Check out our case stories.) Who are our clients? Major owners/operators and main contractors with project values between £1m and £1bn+ globally. Where would I be working? One week you might be working from home. The next, you might travel to the site to meet the construction teams and help organise them. Maybe you’ll pop into our London office for a workshop or a beer. Maybe you’ll fly out to exotic (and sometimes not!) locations in Europe or the Middle East to visit clients. It really depends on what you want to get involved in and what fits with your life. How does what I do connect with the long-term impact on the construction industry? You’re tasked with understanding and solving common problems. We don’t want to reinvent the wheel every time, so you’ll be responsible for documenting new solutions and evolving ones we’ve developed. This goes into our knowledge repository, which we’re going to open source to the industry. The knowledge you capture will be used by us to build new products. You’ll constantly test those products in the field, so we can rapidly iterate and improve them for anyone in the industry to use. ____________________________________________________________ Benefits The standard stuff: - Health Insurance Scheme. Comprehensive private health coverage – for you and your family. Because your well-being is our priority - Pension Scheme. A competitive plan to help you plan for the long term – plus salary sacrifice options available to maximise your savings - Bonus Scheme. As a permanent member of the team, you’ll share in our success. Our annual bonus is designed to reward both the now and the future – with a flexible mix of cash and high-growth equity that you choose. Bonuses are discretionary and based on performance - Professional body membership. One fee covered per year – so you can stay connected to your field and develop your craft - Cycle to Work Scheme. A tax-efficient way to get wheels – and do your bit for the environment The life-changing stuff: - In-house coaching. Regular 1:1 coaching sessions, fully confidential, to help you navigate challenges, build self-awareness, and grow intentionally – professionally and as a human being - Equity upside. As we grow, you grow. Our generous equity scheme is especially powerful for those who stay with us on our journey. You help us build the future – and own a piece of it - Flexible working. Work where it makes sense – most of our team works from home, visiting sites or clients regularly. We care about outcomes, not clock-ins - Relentless development. Our goal is for every year here to be worth five years of development anywhere else. You’ll get a coach, a mentor, honest feedback, and a culture that challenges you to keep levelling up ____________________________________________________________ Important! Applying properly We get thousands of applications so please write us a letter as part of your application explaining: - Why you want to join us - What you’ll bring to the team We aren't a giant, faceless corporation; we really care about the people who want to join our team, so your letter will be read carefully. After that, we’ll reach out to you to schedule a casual conversation to help you get to know us a bit better and tell us a bit about yourself. A couple of technical and personal assessments follow to understand your capability based on our own development matrix. This is to ensure that when you join, you’re starting at the right level of responsibility.

title: Insurance Product Manager / Underwriter (P&C)
descriptionHtml:
Most insurance product roles ask you to perfect one product in one market. This one asks you to build Europe’s SME insurance products: decide what we cover and who we insure, negotiate it with our carriers and get it live, market after market.

Deep in the wording. Fast in the build.

About Insify

Insurance for entrepreneurs is still built the old way: one market at a time, wordings nobody reads, and cover that leaves out the very businesses that need it most.

We're doing it differently.

Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by €43M in total funding from world-class investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years, we've expanded from the Netherlands into France, Germany and Ireland, and we're just getting started. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

We aren't just building a company; we're leading a revolution. Our culture is intense, high-stakes, and mission-driven. We hire smart, ambitious "owners" who possess a relentless drive to win. This is an environment for those who thrive on challenges, value intellectual honesty, and share our mindset of becoming a global category leader.

Our founding team consists of seasoned entrepreneurs who have previously built iconic businesses like HelloFresh, Bloomon, and SumUp. We bring that same bias for speed, scale, and high standards to one of the most structurally broken experiences in financial services. Together, we combine that deep fintech and e-commerce expertise with cutting-edge AI to stay ahead of the curve.


What you’ll own in your first year

You won’t inherit a finished product shelf. You’ll build the engine that fills it.

  1. Build the product engine. Turn how we benchmark a market into a system: compare cover, limits and exclusions across local players, our Dutch home product and our other markets, so every new product starts from facts, not gut feeling.
  2. Make the call on cover. Decide what we cover, what we don’t and who we insure, and turn it into a proposal. The tools do the comparison; the judgment is yours.
  3. Get it signed. Take the proposal to our risk carriers and negotiate it. You know what to push on, what to let go and which clause will set off six red flags.
  4. Get it live. Adapt our wordings to each new market, run the legal review and launch. Less writing from scratch, more making one strong product fit the next market. Then track loss ratios, competition and customer feedback, and sharpen it.
  5. Build what doesn’t exist yet. In the markets where we double down, own custom products from the insurance side, including cover for the trades and businesses others decline.

Who you are

You’re an insurance expert first and a builder second, but a real one.

  • You have 5+ years hands-on in commercial P&C (Property & Casualty) at an insurer, MGA, (re)insurer or specialist broker, across underwriting, product and wordings, ideally for SMEs.
  • You know what is covered, what isn’t and what should be. Hand you a wording from a market you’ve never worked in and you’ll spot the gaps within minutes.
  • You’ve worked across more than one line, product or market, and you can apply what you know to a market you’ve never seen.
  • You’ve sat at the table with insurers or capacity providers and know where the red lines are.
  • You’d rather fix insurance than complain about it. Maybe you already tried: at an insurtech, an MGA, your own startup, or on the carrier side building products with insurtechs.
  • You think like the customer: plain questions, fair cover, and no excluding everything just to be safe.
  • You’re at home in Excel and data, and curious about what automation and LLMs can take off your plate. You don’t need to code; our product and tech teams build the digital journey with you.
  • You work fluently in English; German, French or Dutch is a big plus.

    • What we offer
  • Real ownership. You decide what we cover and work directly with the MT, close to where decisions get made.
  • Range. More products and markets in a year than most people see in a decade at an incumbent.
  • A share in what we build. Equity, so you share in the value you build.
  • A team that cares. We live by four values: Grit, Care, Impact and Entrepreneurship.
  • Growth. Room to grow into leading our insurance product work as we add markets, plus an in-house coaching and leadership program.
  • The package. Competitive salary package + 6% pension, holidays, well-being budget and rich social events (ski trip, summer and winter party).
  • The basics, done well. Office in central Amsterdam, laptop, hybrid working. Relocation support.

    • If you know insurance inside out and you’d rather build products than maintain them, we’d like to meet you. No cover letter needed.

title: Interaction Designer, HCI
descriptionHtml:
About Act

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

Role

You will design the detailed mechanics of how users interact with A1 - the gestures, states, flows, and micro-decisions that determine whether an AI-driven product feels controlled or confusing.

This role is focused on HCI interaction design: how users give input, receive feedback, supervise AI actions, correct mistakes, and maintain agency over AI-driven workflows.

There are no established playbooks for interaction design in proactive AI products. You will help define new patterns from the ground up.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design detailed interaction models for AI-driven flows, including how users initiate, monitor, pause, correct, and complete multi-step tasks.

  • Define interaction states for AI interfaces: idle, thinking, acting, waiting, uncertain, interrupted, failed, and recovered.

  • Design human-in-the-loop controls - how users review AI decisions, override actions, and stay informed without micromanaging.

  • Create interaction patterns for delegation, approval, correction, escalation, reversibility, and recovery.

  • Create detailed interaction specifications, annotated flows, and prototypes for engineering handoff.

  • Work with product and ML teams to translate system capabilities and constraints into usable interaction patterns.

  • Test interaction designs with real users to identify where AI behavior creates confusion, distrust, or friction.

  • Contribute to a shared library of HCI interaction patterns that can be reused across the product.

What You Will Need

  • Experience as an interaction designer or senior UX designer with strong interaction design depth.

  • Ability to design at the micro level - states, transitions, edge cases, and failure handling.

  • Strong prototyping skills in Figma or equivalent tools.

  • Systematic thinking - able to map complex AI behavior into coherent user-facing interaction logic.

  • Clear understanding of HCI principles: user control, transparency, feedback, and graceful recovery.

  • Experience working closely with engineers to ensure interactions are implemented as designed.

  • Comfort designing for systems where output is non-deterministic and behavior can vary across sessions.

  • Strong judgment on when users should be guided, interrupted, asked for confirmation, or left alone.

 

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product

 

Interview process

For design roles, we expect candidates to submit a portfolio as part of the application process.

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2 rounds of interviews and a design assessment.

Applications are evaluated by our team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us. This isn't just a job offer; it's an invitation to be part of a team that's bringing AI to have practical benefits to billions globally.

descriptionHtml:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The role is fundamentally about problem solving: understanding business challenges, breaking them down, and delivering pragmatic, scalable solutions.

You’ll work closely with product, analytics, and engineering teams, operating with a high degree of autonomy. That means proactively gathering context, aligning stakeholders, and ensuring work lands effectively.

Data Platform sits at the centre of the business, with a real opportunity to shape how teams interact with data. The focus is on enabling fast, iterative analytics, moving from idea to insight quickly, while maintaining strong foundations around reliability, cost, and security.

  • Experience building data-intensive systems

  • Strong problem solver who focuses on understanding before building

  • Good judgement on build vs buy decisions

  • Comfortable working in ambiguity and shaping direction

  • Clear communicator across technical and non-technical audiences

  • Able to manage multiple streams of work without losing momentum

  • Pragmatic, balancing speed with scalability and reliability

  • Actively looks to improve ways of working, including leveraging AI tooling

title: Junior Software Developer
descriptionHtml:
The Software Developer I, Connector role supports Trial Interactive’s proprietary platform, Connector - the cloud-based integrations that move life science data between clients’ clinical systems (for example EDC/eCRF and IRT systems) and Trial Interactive’s life science products. Working under the guidance of senior engineers, the role helps build and maintain connectors, keeps client data flowing accurately, and resolves issues when it does not.

This is a blended role, covering development and maintenance up until handling client requests. This role works closely with the Solutions, DevOps and Engineering teams.

DESCRIPTION

As part of the Development and maintenance responsibility, the resource handles:

• Develop, test and maintain connector components in C# on .NET (AWS Lambda), including the parsers and mappers that convert source-system data (API payloads, files) into the formats required by the Trial Interactive CTMS and eTMF.

• Configure and extend mappings for new studies, sites and visit/status definitions on existing connectors, reusing existing modules wherever possible.

• Assist in the technical onboarding of new clients and studies: connector configuration, test runs in non-production environments, and verification before go-live.

• Work with the AWS services connectors are built on (Lambda, SQS, S3, EventBridge/Step Functions, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch) and make small, reviewed infrastructure changes using Terraform under supervision.

• Consume, test and troubleshoot REST APIs (client/vendor APIs and Trial Interactive import APIs) using code and tools such as Postman, and help extend APIs that improve connector stability and connectivity.

• Write unit and functional tests; use Git (feature branches, merge requests, environment branches) and follow the team’s code review and release process.

• Keep code, configuration and change records documented so that others can maintain them.

• Work on special projects, such as local test environments using LocalStack.

As part of handling Client communication, support and ticket resolution, the resource does:

• Own assigned support tickets from triage to closure: reproduce the issue, investigate, fix or escalate, and record the outcome in the ticketing system (for example Jira, ServiceDesk Plus).

• Investigate data issues end to end – trace a record from the source payload through the archive, parser, connector database and logs to its CTMS/eTMF import result – and establish the root cause (RCA) with evidence.

• Reconcile source-system data against the CTMS/eTMF when a client reports missing or mismatched subjects, visits or statuses, and explain any differences.

• Communicate with clients and Solutions Engineers by email, tickets and calls: acknowledge requests promptly, ask clear clarifying questions, give regular status updates, and explain findings and next steps in plain language.

• Monitor connector health (CloudWatch logs, failed imports, notifications) and respond to failures within agreed response times.

• Escalate appropriately to senior engineers, DevOps or the vendor, with a concise summary of what happened, when, in which environment and for which records.

• Write up RCAs, fixes and known issues so that repeat problems are resolved faster, and help keep support documentation current.

• Handle client and clinical data with care: use the minimum data needed, never share one client’s information with another, and follow Trial Interactive data-protection and change-control procedures.

General

• Keep learning the connector platform, the clinical-trial data domain and cloud and software development best practices.

• Complete all other tasks that are deemed appropriate for this role and assigned by the manager/supervisor.


REQUIRED SKILLS

• Clear written and spoken English, with the ability to explain technical issues in plain language to non-technical clients and to write concise ticket updates and emails.

• A client-service mindset: responsive, calm under pressure, and takes ownership of a ticket until it is resolved or properly handed over.

• Strong problem-solving and debugging skills: forms a hypothesis, checks logs and data, and proves the root cause with evidence before concluding.

• Strong attention to detail with data, such as identifiers, dates, time zones and character encodings.

• Good time management: balances planned development work with interrupt-driven support, prioritizing by client impact.

• Works collaboratively within a team, asks for help early, and is self-motivated and eager to learn.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor’s degree or its equivalent in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

• 0–1 years of experience in software development, technical support or cloud-based application support; internships and substantial academic or personal projects count.

• Working knowledge of C# and the .NET framework: able to read and debug existing code and deliver small features.

• Familiarity with AWS, particularly Lambda, S3, SQS and CloudWatch Logs.

• Working SQL skills (joins, filtering, aggregation) on relational databases, preferably MySQL.

• Understanding of REST APIs and of JSON, XML and CSV data; experience calling APIs with Postman or similar tools.

• Understanding of data parsing and mapping techniques, including handling of dates, null values and encodings.

• Experience or familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git).

DESIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

• Experience with LocalStack for local AWS cloud application development.

• Familiarity with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code tools.

• Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation.

• Prior experience in customer-facing support, or with ticketing tools such as Jira or ServiceDesk Plus.

• Exposure to clinical research systems and concepts (EDC, CTMS, eTMF; study, site, subject, visit) or to regulated (GxP) software environments.

• Scripting (Python or shell) for data checks and log analysis.

• Familiarity with containerization and microservices architecture.

title: Junior TechOps Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Hozah

Hozah makes parking automatic. Our cameras recognise your car when you arrive and payment happens by itself when you leave. No apps, no machines, no tickets. We were named PayTech Company of the Year, we sit in Deloitte's list of the 50 fastest growing tech companies in the UK, and we are expanding our estate of automated car parks across the country.

Every site runs on ANPR cameras, payment kiosks, edge devices and 4G connectivity, and all of it has to work around the clock. The TechOps team keeps that estate healthy, and we are looking for a junior engineer to join it.

The role

You will be hands-on from day one, helping to monitor, maintain and fix the technology running in car parks across the country. When a camera drops offline, a kiosk misbehaves or a site stops reporting data, you will be part of the team that works out why and puts it right, usually remotely.

You will learn a genuinely broad set of skills in one role: networking, IoT devices, monitoring, APIs, databases and cloud systems, all on a live estate where your work has visible impact the same day. You will be coached and supported as you grow, with clear standards, documented processes and experienced engineers around you.

What you'll be doing

  • Monitoring the health of cameras, kiosks and network equipment across 150+ car parks, and acting when something looks wrong.

  • Diagnosing and fixing faults across devices, networks and our backend platform, working through problems methodically.

  • Preparing, configuring and shipping hardware for new sites, and supporting site launches.

  • Keeping inventory, configuration records and documentation accurate and up to date.

  • Managing your tickets in Jira with clear notes, sensible prioritisation and proper follow-through.

  • Learning constantly: from the TechOps team, from our developers, and from the estate itself.

What we're looking for

This is a junior role. We care more about fundamentals, honesty and appetite to learn than years of experience.

  • Around 1–2 years of hands-on experience in IT support, infrastructure or technical operations, or strong fundamentals you can demonstrate from projects, a home lab or study.

  • Networking basics you can explain in plain English: what a switch and a router do, what an IP address is, what a VPN is for.

  • A structured instinct when something goes offline: check power, check the network, check the device, in that order.

  • Some awareness of APIs and SQL. You do not need to be fluent; knowing what they are and wanting to use them is enough.

  • Solid Windows knowledge: event logs, command line, system configuration.

  • Organised, reliable and calm when something breaks on a live site.

What this role isn't

  • Corporate IT support. The users of our systems are cameras and cars, and the work is looking after a distributed technology estate.

  • A narrow role. You will touch hardware, networking, software and data in the same week.

  • A dead end. The team is growing, the estate is growing, and there is a clear path to more senior TechOps work as you develop.

Salary, location and working pattern

  • 4 days a week in our Croydon office, 1 day from home, with occasional site visits.

  • Free breakfast, lunch, drinks and snacks in the office, excellent transport links, and two friendly office dogs.

  • You will need the right to work in the UK. A full UK driving licence is handy for site visits.

title: Kfz-Prüfingenieur mit Betrauung (m/w/d) – mit Perspektive zum Abteilungsleiter
descriptionHtml:
Beschreibung

Sie sind betrauter Kfz-Prüfingenieur und möchten nicht nur prüfen, sondern mittelfristig Verantwortung übernehmen? Dann bieten wir Ihnen einen Weg, auf dem Sie in Ruhe in eine Führungsrolle hineinwachsen.

Wir sind die von Hebel Fahrzeugtechnik GmbH. Wir betreiben eigene GTÜ-Prüfstellen in Lüneburg, Lauenburg/Elbe und Hamburg und führen als Partner der GTÜ Gesellschaft für Technische Überwachung mbH amtliche Fahrzeuguntersuchungen durch.

Gut zu wissen: Wir arbeiten eng mit dem von Hebel Ingenieurbüro zusammen – einem etablierten Kfz-Sachverständigenbüro, das professionelle Unfall- und Haftpflichtgutachten für Privat- und Geschäftskunden erstellt. Für Sie bedeutet das: ein breites fachliches Umfeld über die Prüftätigkeit hinaus.

Warum wir jetzt suchen: Wir planen langfristig. Die Leitung unserer Prüfstellen und des ca. zehnköpfigen Teams soll in einigen Jahren in neue Hände übergehen – und wir möchten die Person dafür frühzeitig an Bord holen. Sie steigen zunächst als Prüfingenieur ein, lernen unser Team, unsere Standorte und Abläufe kennen und übernehmen dann Schritt für Schritt mehr Verantwortung. Für die Einarbeitung nehmen wir uns bewusst Zeit.

Ihr Einsatzgebiet: Unsere Standorte Lüneburg, Lauenburg/Elbe und Hamburg.

Ihr Weg in die Führungsposition

Kein Sprung ins kalte Wasser, sondern ein geplanter Übergang in Ihrem Tempo:

  • Ankommen: Prüftätigkeit an unseren Standorten, Kennenlernen von Team, Kunden, Abläufen und der Zusammenarbeit mit der GTÜ

  • Verantwortung übernehmen: erste Aufgaben der fachlichen und organisatorischen Leitung, z. B. Qualitätssicherung, Einarbeitung neuer Kolleginnen und Kollegen, fachliche Ansprechperson im Team

  • Übergabe: Stellvertretung der jetzigen Führungskraft und anschließend vollständige Übernahme der Position

Zuständigkeiten / Hauptaufgaben

Von Beginn an:

  • Durchführung von Untersuchungen der periodischen Fahrzeugüberwachung (HU/SP)

  • Abgasuntersuchungen (AU)

  • Änderungsabnahmen nach §19(3) StVZO

  • Wenn bereits Qualifizierung vorliegt: Begutachtungen im Rahmen des Technischen Dienstes, z. B. für Sondereintragungen, Umbauten und Importfahrzeuge

  • Tätigkeit im Außen- und Innendienst

Schrittweise hinzukommen:

  • fachliche Qualitätssicherung und Einhaltung der amtlichen Vorgaben an allen Standorten

  • fachliche Anleitung, Einarbeitung und Schulung des Teams

  • Ansprechperson für die GTÜ, z. B. bei Audits und fachlichen Rückfragen

  • Ansprechperson für unsere Kunden: Großkunden, Fuhrparks, Werkstätten, Autohäuser oder Einzelkunden

  • Mitwirkung an Dienstplanung, Prüfausstattung und der Weiterentwicklung unserer Abläufe

Qualifikationen / Anforderungen

  • Betrauung zum Kfz-Prüfingenieur – gern auch von einer anderen Überwachungsorganisation, den Wechsel zur GTÜ begleiten wir

  • Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung

  • Interesse daran, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und ein Team fachlich zu führen

  • Sorgfalt, Zuverlässigkeit und ein hoher Qualitätsanspruch

  • Freude am Umgang mit Kunden und Kollegen

  • Bereitschaft zum Einsatz an unseren Standorten

Was noch fehlt, bauen wir gemeinsam auf

Sie haben noch keine Führungserfahrung oder sehen bei sich selbst noch Entwicklungsbedarf? Kein Problem – genau dafür planen wir die lange Einarbeitung ein. Wir schauen gemeinsam, where Sie stehen, und entwickeln Sie gezielt weiter:

  • individueller Plan mit regelmäßigen Entwicklungsgesprächen

  • Weiterbildungen zu Führungs-, Kommunikations- und Konfliktmanagement

  • fachliche Weiterbildungen, z. B. zum Unterschriftsberechtigten des Technischen Dienstes oder zum Kfz-Sachverständigen (inkl. IfS-Zertifizierung)

  • In-House-Schulungen – keine Anreise nötig, flexible Terminplanung

  • Einarbeitung durch erfahrene Kollegen, die ihr Wissen gerne weitergeben

Leistungen der Anstellung

  • Unbefristete Festanstellung bei der von Hebel Fahrzeugtechnik GmbH

  • Grundgehalt ab 4.000 €/Monat (Vollzeit) – je nach Erfahrung und Qualifikation mehr; mit wachsender Verantwortung entwickelt sich selbstverständlich auch Ihr Gehalt weiter

  • Eine langfristige Perspektive mit klarer Entwicklung zur Führungsposition

  • Arbeit an modernem Prüf-Equipment

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und planbare Einsatzorte per Dienstplan

  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge

  • Ein Team mit sympathischen Kollegen und familiärer Arbeitsweise

  • Mitarbeiter Boni über Probonio

  • Gemeinsame Events wie Weihnachtsfeiern u. v. m.

Kontakte

Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Bewerbung mit Lebenslauf und möglichem Eintrittstermin. Schreiben Sie uns gerne auch, wo Sie sich noch weiterentwickeln möchten.

Bewerben Sie sich mit dem Button auf dieser Seite.

About Sona

Running a frontline business is an operational puzzle most software has never touched. Shift-by-shift labour costs, compliance that changes by region and by role, and margins thin enough that a badly built rota can sink a quarter. It's a harder problem than most white-collar SaaS, and yet frontline sectors employ 80% of the global workforce and have received about 1% of the last decade's software investment.

We think that's because the problem needed AI, not just better software, before it was solvable. Frontline organisations sit on enormous amounts of operational data. Used properly, that data lets agents take on real parts of running the business rather than just reporting on it. That's what we're building at Sona, and it's early enough that the systems you build now will still be foundational in three years.

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here.

About the Role

Sona's Labour AI team builds the forecasting, rules and scheduling tools that help hospitality and retail businesses get staffing right. This role is about getting that tooling to work for a specific site: its trading patterns, its staff, its quirks. You'll work directly with customers to turn Sona's tools into labour models that are used on site and have a huge impact.

You'll derive labour rules from real trading data, spend time on site with customer teams to learn how the business runs, and build the trust with site managers. You'll present the impact and ROI of that work to customer executives and general managers, and act as the subject matter expert for labour optimisation in sales conversations.

You'll also be the person site managers trust enough to change how they staff, and the person customer executives and General Managers trust enough to back the changes you're proposing. You'll need as much influence as analysis to make that work. You'll report back to customer leadership on the impact, in numbers they can take to their own board.

You'll adapt the same underlying labour model across different business types, from QSR to premium dining to retail.

Responsibilities

  • Derive labour rules from real trading data using Sona's tooling and your own operational knowledge

  • Spend time on site with customer teams, learning practical realities like stock deliveries and close-down procedures

  • Build trust with site managers so workload models actually get followed

  • Present impact and ROI to customer executives and general managers, winning buy-in for operational change

  • Act as the labour optimisation subject matter expert in sales conversations

  • Work across the full portfolio of live customer projects, picking up work as priorities shift between accounts

Requirements

  • An operational background in hospitality, retail, or a similar hourly-workforce, fluctuating-demand business. You understand how the business runs day to day, not just how to analyse it from the outside

  • Confident presenting to and winning buy-in from customer executives, general managers and boards, and comfortable holding your own with competing agendas in the room

  • Comfortable with technology and confident picking up new tools quickly, including using AI tools in your own workflow

  • Able to look into the data yourself and make decisions from what you find

  • Comfortable operating without a fixed playbook

  • Excited about using AI in your day-to-day work to 10x your output

  • Bonus: a retail or workforce-management background where the underlying concepts transfer to hospitality

Bonus: a commercial finance background with genuine credibility in front of operators

We're a hybrid working team you can expect to work 2+ days/week in our London office (Soho), and 2+ days/week on site with customers.

  • 35 days annual leave (25 days standard plus 10 flexible public holiday days)

  • Salary sacrifice childcare scheme (Workplace Nursery)

  • Annual all expenses paid team retreats

  • The latest Macbook and equipment budget for your home office

  • Professional development budget

Note: this represents a typical benefits package for a UK-based, full-time employee. Exact details may vary based on location and employment type but we try to be as fair as possible to all of our team members. Please ask your contact in the Talent team to clarify the available benefits for you.

title: Lead AI Product Manager - Telematics
descriptionHtml:
About Zego 🚀

At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.

Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive.

We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖

For us, AI isn't a line on a roadmap or a buzzword on a slide. It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook.

We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers.

Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor.

If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring.

About the Role

We are looking for a Lead AI Product Manager to own Telematics at Zego. Our proprietary telematics is how we understand the way people actually drive, and the ratings it produces shape pricing, risk management and claims across our whole book.

You’ll own the telematics stack as a product: the SDKs that capture driving data, the processing that turns it into trips, events and scores, and the Risk Management capabilities that act on them. You’ll set the 6-12 month direction across these teams and make the build-vs-buy-vs-partner calls on sensors, data sources and models.

You’ll work closely with Data Science, Pricing, Claims and Zego’s Leadership Team, champion an experiment-first culture, and mentor Product Managers across the organisation.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Set the six-to-12-month Telematics strategy across the SDKs, data processing and Risk Management, including the build, buy or partner calls on sensors, data and models.

  • Own data quality at the source, setting the standards for trip recording, location accuracy, battery impact and stability that every score depends on.

  • Own the product side of our scoring models with Data Science, so the score is accurate, explainable and safe to change on a live book.

  • Lead Risk Management, defining how we act on driving behaviour - from price adjustments to interventions and cancellations - balancing loss ratio with fair customer outcomes.

  • Turn driving data into P&L impact with Pricing, Underwriting, Claims and Fraud, through sharper risk selection, fairer prices and better fraud detection.

  • Embed rigorous experimentation as the default operating rhythm, even when changes touch price and live policies.

  • Build reusable AI playbooks, workflows and assets that multiply the whole team’s output, from trip-data analysis to automated data and model monitoring.

  • Coach Product Managers across the organisation, raising the bar for product craft and data capability.

What You’ll Need to Be Successful

  • Strategic product leadership. Significant experience leading product strategy across multiple teams or domains in a high-growth environment, with decisions that moved business-level metrics.

  • Data, sensor or ML products. You’ve built products on behavioural, location or sensor data - ideally telematics, mobility or IoT - and understand how signals become models, and models become decisions.

  • Technical depth. Comfortable engaging engineers on mobile SDKs, data pipelines and ML pipelines, enough to make informed strategic bets.

  • Commercial and risk fluency. Deep understanding of pricing levers, risk modelling and loss ratios, and credible with Actuarial, Finance and Leadership.

  • Data mastery. You are as comfortable in Snowflake as you are in a strategy review, and you can interrogate model performance, not just read a dashboard.

  • Experiment-first operator. You have built experiment cultures, not just run individual tests.

  • You work AI-first. You will use AI daily here, and we mean daily. You do not need to arrive an expert, but you do need to arrive curious, experiment fast, and take ownership of getting good quickly. People who wait to be trained will find this uncomfortable.

The Zego ways of working 🏡

Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: some of us are in our office (central London, Gibraltar or Halifax) weekly, others monthly or quarterly. It's about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.

We also make a point of getting everyone in the same room. Teams come together every quarter, and once a year the whole company does, properly. It's a serious investment and consistently one of the best parts of the year.

Here is what the last one looked like.

Benefits 🎁

💰 Market-competitive salary, benchmarked against your function and reviewed every year.

🏆 Annual performance bonus, linked to company performance and your contribution.

📈 Share options, a real stake in the company and a share in the future you build

🩺 Private medical insurance.

🏖️ Pension, generous holiday, and £1,000 a year to spend on getting to the office or learning something new.

💻 Cutting-edge systems and tools, so you always have what you need to drive your impact.

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? We want to hear from you.

Zego, leading the AI evolution in insurance.

Equal opportunities 🌈

We're an equal opportunity employer and we value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability status.

descriptionHtml:

You'll own the methodology that drives successful Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) engagements, accelerating customer adoption, getting high-value workflows into production, and enabling customers to become independent builders.

To achieve this, you'll focus on four key areas:

  • Measure engagement success through workflows deployed to production, customer adoption improvements, and measurable business outcomes, rather than services delivery alone.

Scale Delivery Quality & Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Partner with the Partner Delivery Manager and Partnerships teams to ensure external delivery partners follow the same engagement methodology and quality standards.

  • Help define readiness, certification, and quality expectations for partner Deployment Strategists to enable consistent customer experiences at scale.

  • Work closely with FDEs, Product, and Engineering to turn customer feedback, technical gaps, feature requests, and custom integration needs into actionable product insights.

REQUIREMENTS

Must-haves

  • 🤝 Enterprise Customer Experience: You have 7+ years of experience in customer-facing roles such as professional services, solutions consulting, implementation, or customer success within a software company.

  • 🌟 People Leadership: You have 2+ years of experience leading, coaching, and developing customer-facing teams, with a track record of building high-performing teams.

  • 🚀 0-to-1 Builder Experience: You've built or scaled a deployment, implementation, or professional services function and know how to create structure and repeatable processes in an evolving environment.

  • 💼 Executive Stakeholder Management: You're experienced in leading executive discovery, building compelling ROI cases, and securing buy-in from multiple stakeholders within enterprise organizations.

  • 🛠️ Technical Fluency: You're comfortable discussing workflow automation, integrations, and AI use cases with technical stakeholders and collaborating closely with engineers without needing to write code yourself.

  • 📊 Operational Excellence: You know how to define success metrics, build scalable methodologies, and turn customer engagement learnings into actionable playbooks.

  • 🎯 Customer Outcome Mindset: You're focused on driving measurable customer adoption and long-term value, rather than simply delivering projects or completing engagements.

Nice-to-haves

  • ⚡ Automation Platforms: You're familiar with n8n or other workflow automation, integration, or low-code platforms.

  • 🔄 Change Management: You have experience helping enterprise organizations drive adoption, navigate organizational change, and embed new technologies into their ways of working.

  • 🤝 Partner Ecosystems: You've worked with systems integrators, consulting firms, or external delivery partners to deliver customer implementations or technical engagements.

Why join us?

At n8n, you'll have the opportunity to build a brand-new function at the heart of how we scale enterprise customer adoption. You won't just manage a team — you'll shape how we engage customers, demonstrate the value of automation, and turn high-impact use cases into production workflows that drive lasting business outcomes.

You'll work closely with leaders across Customer Success, Sales, Product, and Engineering, with significant visibility and influence over our enterprise growth strategy. As one of Europe's fastest-growing startups, we offer the opportunity to build from the ground up, experiment with new approaches, and create a scalable deployment model that helps customers become independent, successful builders.

You'll join a supportive, remote-first team that values autonomy, collaboration, and continuous learning, where your impact will be visible from day one.

Sound like a challenge you're excited to take on?

Apply now — and help us build the future of automation.

n8n is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We can sponsor visas to Germany; for any other country, you need to have existing right to work.

Our company language is English.

You care about diversity and inclusion? We do too! Check out our Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging initiatives at n8n (https://www.notion.so/n8n/Diversity-inclusion-and-belonging-n8n-c1bec2fff536422d868b1a438d990e35).

Please apply to the location you're the most likely to work from in the future.

Benefits

  • Ownership 💪 – Our core value is to “empower others,” and we mean it—you’ll get a slice of n8n with equity.

  • Work/life balance 🏖️ – We work hard but ensure you have time to recharge:

title: Lead Machine Learning Scientist, Business Banking
descriptionHtml:
🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us. 

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

📍London/Cardiff/UK Remote | 💰 £115,000 - £150,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits  ✨

About our Machine Learning Business Banking team

Our mission in Business Banking is to simplify banking for small businesses; making business banking fairer, simpler and more transparent. Monzo Business Banking is fast-growing, is the UK’s most recommended business account for overall service quality. We recently hit 1 million customers and are used by 1 in 6 UK SMEs.

We want to help businesses spend less time on financial admin and more time focused on running and growing their business. We’re building intelligent, data-driven and AI/ML-enabled product experiences that help small businesses feel more in control, make better decisions, and get more value from Monzo.

ML is at the core of how we build and scale our products, enabling Monzo to make better decisions, faster, and helping us serve businesses more effectively.

As a Lead Machine Learning Scientist in Business Banking, you’ll help build and ship models that power the next generation of Business Banking experiences. You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, Research, Data Science and Analytics Engineering to bring ML-enabled product capability into the heart of how we build for businesses.

Whether it’s helping businesses understand their cash flow, reducing manual admin, surfacing the right insight at the right moment, or helping teams build intelligent product experiences responsibly, our work makes business banking smarter, simpler and more useful for SMEs.

What you'll be working on

As a Lead Machine Learning Scientist, you’ll be a technical leader and hands-on individual contributor, spearheading our ML and GenAI capabilities and shipping key models that powers magical Business Banking experiences.

You’ll:

  • Be one of the first ML Scientists in Business Banking, bringing leadership through ambiguity by adding structure and direction to our ML capabilities while staying agile and building momentum.
  • Develop and deploy advanced ML models on our cloud-native data platform to serve hundreds of thousands of business customers.
  • Partner with Product, data science and other stakeholders to identify the highest-impact opportunities, size impact, and define success metrics.
  • Decide when to use ML, GenAI, or simpler approaches and be clear on trade-offs.
  • Design robust evaluation and monitoring so we can ship responsibly and measure impact in production.
  • Lead the design and implementation of batch and near-real-time models (e.g. LLM-powered experiences, predictive models, time-series forecasting).
  • Collaborate closely with MLOps and Backend Engineering to operationalise models end-to-end and raise the bar on ML lifecycle rigor.
  • Set technical standards, mentor others, and support experimentation and iteration.

You should apply if

What we’re doing here at Monzo excites you!

  • You have a multiple year track record of excellence leading the development and deployment of advanced Machine Learning models to tackle real business problems, preferably in a fast-moving tech company.
  • You have experience developing and shipping state-of-the-art ML models to production and delivering business impact.
  • You're impact-driven and excited to own the end-to-end journey that starts with a business problem and ends with your solution having a measurable impact in production.
  • You have a self-starter mindset; you proactively identify issues and opportunities and tackle them without being told to do so.
  • You speak Python fluently and have extensive, hands-on experience with scikit-learn. You are comfortable using SQL, and keen to learn Go, which is used in many of our backend microservices.
  • You’re comfortable working in a team that deals with ambiguity and have experience helping your team and stakeholders resolve that ambiguity.
  • You want to be involved in building a product that small businesses use to run and manage their financial lives every day.
  • You have a product mindset: you care about customer outcomes and you want to make data-informed decisions.
  • You’re excited about fast-moving developments in Machine Learning and AI and can communicate those ideas to colleagues who are not familiar with the domain.
  • You’re adaptable, curious and enjoy learning new technologies and ideas.
  • You’re excited by the opportunity to help Business Banking evolve into AI and ML-enabled product capability.
  • You can work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, Research and Data colleagues to shape product strategy, clarify trade-offs and build things that customers actually use.
  • You’re thoughtful about responsible ML/AI; especially in financial products where trust, transparency and customer control matter.

Nice to haves

  • Experience working on personalisation, ranking, recommendation, forecasting, classification or decisioning problems for customer-facing applications.
  • Experience working on ML systems for fintech, banking, accounting, payments, lending, invoicing, cash flow, tax, risk or business software.
  • Experience with GenAI, LLMs, agentic workflows, retrieval, evaluation frameworks, or human-in-the-loop product experiences.
  • Commercial experience writing critical production code and working with microservices.
  • Experience designing experiments, A/B tests or other approaches to measure product and customer impact.
  • Experience working in regulated environments or with products where explainability, auditability and customer trust are especially important.

The interview process

Our interview process involves 3 main stages. We promise not to ask you any brain teasers or trick questions!

30 minute recruiter call

45 minute call with hiring manager

Full Loop: ML Modelling Interview, Product & ML interview, Behavioural Interview, Leadership interview

Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability. You will have the chance to speak to our recruitment team at various points during your process but if you do have any specific questions ahead of this please contact us on

What’s in it for you

✈️ We can help you relocate to the UK

✅ We can sponsor visas

📍This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London).

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team.

📚Learning budget of £1,000 a year for training courses and conferences

➕And much more, see our full list of benefits here

If you prefer to work part-time, we'll make this happen whenever we can - whether this is to help you meet other commitments or strike a great work-life balance

#LI-REMOTE #LI-SR1

Equal opportunities for everyone

Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our blog, 2026 Diversity and Inclusion Report and 2025 Gender Pay Gap Report.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.

If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊

title: Lead / Principal Engineer - Full Stack
descriptionHtml:
A different kind of organisation

  • High trust, transparency, and autonomy
  • Small teams, high ownership, flat structures
  • Radical compensation transparency
  • Sense of ownership in collective success
  • Work with exceptional people who deeply care about their craft

The role

As a Principal Consultant, you're often the first person a customer meets to brainstorm a business problem. You should be at home debating distributed systems with engineers and framing decisions with leadership. You'll frame the problem with customers, shape the approach with the team, provide technical direction, and stay hands-on through delivery. You will work in self-managing, experienced, small, and high-impact teams, solving hard problems. This is a consulting & tech delivery role  and while you will not have direct reports, you will regularly influence teams, mentor practitioners, manage stakeholders, and guide organisations through complex technology and business decisions.

What the work looks like

We can't promise which problem you'll pick up, but the menu right now looks something like this:

  • Redesign a ClickHouse schema so an ad buyer can query 85 billion rows in under two seconds, and discover that pre-exploding the rows 168x is actually the right answer.
  • Keep a vehicle telemetry platform moving billions of messages a day without the Kafka consumers falling over.
  • Build the engineering spine of a mobile wallet used by more than two billion people across four continents.
  • Ship the data product behind peer-review submissions for one of the world's largest scientific publishers.

The list changes every quarter. The pattern doesn't: data-heavy, distributed, and often sitting on top of something that already exists and isn't perfect.

What you'll do

Frame Problems & Propose Solutions

  • Help customers find the right problem before jumping to a solution.
  • Facilitate discovery sessions, architecture reviews, and technical workshops.
  • Translate business goals into a technology strategy and an execution plan.

Lead Through Technical Excellence

  • Stay hands-on; contribute directly to design, architecture, implementation, and review.
  • Make pragmatic calls balancing business needs, engineering quality, and delivery timelines.
  • Guide teams to build scalable, resilient, secure systems  and the practices that keep them that way.

Influence, Advise, and align

  • Act as a trusted advisor on technology and investment decisions; assessments, due diligence, advisory.
  • Build trust and alignment across Sahaj and customer teams
  • Converge competing priorities into a path forward.
  • Communicate complex ideas clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Shape new work through discovery and proposals; mentor others and raise the bar as you go.

Operate Across Technology Domains

Distributed systems, data engineering, AI & agentic systems, DevOps/SRE. Depth in few areas; breadth across, and appreciation for trade-offs in context.

You'll thrive here if

  • You reach for the simplest solution that gets the job done and distrust accidental complexity.
  • You think in systems, not isolated parts.
  • You stay calm when the path is unclear and build clarity for those around you.
  • You move easily between the org-level picture and the technical detail.
  • You're curious by default and pick up new domains fast.
  • You'd rather be in the room with a customer solving a real problem.

What we're looking for

  • Demonstrable building software systems in complex environments.
  • Strong engineering fundamentals; expert in at least one language, ideally polyglot.
  • Hands-on experience designing and delivering distributed systems at scale.
  • Deep grasp of architecture, system design, and engineering trade-offs.
  • Direct experience working with customers and business stakeholders.

What will you experience in terms of culture at Sahaj?

  • A culture of trust, respect and transparency
  • Opportunity to collaborate with some of the finest minds in the industry
  • Work across multiple domains

What are the benefits of being at Sahaj?

  • Unlimited leaves
  • Life insurance & private health insurance
  • No hierarchy
  • Open Salaries

title: Lead Product Manager - CDI Paris - Theodo RetailTech
descriptionHtml:
L’histoire du groupe Theodo et son succès Theodo accompagne depuis 2009 les entreprises innovantes dans la conception, le développement et le déploiement de produits digitaux ingénieux - tels que la plateforme TF1+, l'application LCL Pro ou l'application France Identité Numérique - en tirant parti du meilleur de la technologie et de l’approche Lean. Theodo connait une croissance exceptionnelle depuis 15 ans : nos équipes rassemblent plus de 750 Theodoers, principalement des Software Engineers, passionnés de technologie et d’amélioration continue. En 2025, le groupe Theodo génère 100M€ de CA. La practice RetailTech regroupe nos clients du retail et de l'e-commerce : des acteurs qui transforment l'expérience d'achat de millions d'utilisateurs, en magasin comme en ligne. Elle rassemble les équipes produit, tech et design qui les accompagnent au quotidien sur des programmes à fort enjeu business. C'est un domaine en pleine structuration : on y construit la communauté produit, on outille le staffing, on anime les rituels collectifs (all-hands, dojos) et on contribue aux avant-ventes pour faire grandie le portefeuille.
Tes futures missions : En tant que Lead Product Manager, tu pilotes des projets produits complexes en portant la vision produit, en orchestrant le delivery et en garantissant la création de valeur pour le client comme pour les équipes. - Définir et porter la stratégie produit avec le client : modélisation de la valeur, architecture produit, EPICs, arbitrage des trade-offs et alignement technico-fonctionnel. - Assurer un delivery réussi en coordonnant plusieurs squads pour livrer des projets complexes dans les temps, le budget et le niveau de qualité attendu. - Créer les conditions de réussite des équipes en définissant le bon set-up (équipes Theodo ou partenaires), en négociant les moyens nécessaires et en adaptant l’organisation aux contraintes du projet. - Apporter de la visibilité et de la clarté via des dispositifs de gouvernance adaptés, pour aligner l’ensemble des parties prenantes. -Selon la composition de l'équipe, tu pourras être responsable de faire monter en compétence les Products Managers, en créant un environnement propice à leur réussite, leur montée en compétences et leur projection chez le client et/ou chez Theodo. - Garantir la satisfaction client sur le long terme, en construisant une relation de confiance, en identifiant de nouvelles opportunités et en collaborant avec les équipes Sales, Staffing et People. Les problématiques et les technos sont très différentes d’un projet à l’autre, voici quelques exemples : - iDealwine® : leader mondial des enchères de vins en ligne a engagé la migration de son site e-commerce monolithique vers une architecture composable pour gagner en évolutivité, en sécurité et en maîtrise technologique. Après 2 mois de cadrage, les équipes Theodo ont piloté une approche design-to-cost permettant de modulariser la plateforme et de migrer 20 ans d’historique en 14 mois, dans le respect du budget et du planning. - Sevetys : refonte complète d’une web app métier avec deux volets stratégiques : un outil de prise de rendez-vous pour les propriétaires d’animaux et un back-office dédié aux vétérinaires. Deux équipes produit ont piloté la reconstruction des plateformes de bout en bout, rejointes en fin de projet par une équipe data pour structurer et valoriser les données. Principal défi : une mise en production coordonnée à grande échelle, impliquant de nombreuses cliniques vétérinaires, sans interruption d’activité. Tes perspectives d'évolution : Les voies qui s’ouvrent à toi ensuite : - devenir Group PM et manager les Lead PM d'un grand compte - t’orienter vers un rôle plus commercial sur d’autres grands comptes : Key Account Manager - mettre ton expertise de gestion de projets complexes à profit dans un rôle de COO ou CPO Une méthodologie basée sur l’apprentissage continu : Chez Theodo, nous avons construit notre approche tech autour d’une conviction forte : on développe d’abord les personnes, avant de développer les produits. Notre Lean Tech® System met l’accent sur l’apprentissage continu : tu évolueras dans un environnement qui investit sur le long terme, où l’objectif est de te permettre de progresser chaque jour, tout en construisant des produits utiles et performants pour nos clients. Profil recherché : - Diplômé·e d’une grande école d’ingénieur, avec plus de 5 ans d’expérience professionnelle, dont au moins 4 ans en product management (Senior PM / Lead PM / Head of Product), en startup, ESN ou cabinet de conseil. - Intérêt marqué pour la conception de produits à fort impact business, avec une appétence pour la tech et de bonnes connaissances sur le sujet. - Excellente aisance relationnelle et client : capable de créer une relation de confiance, d’échanger avec des interlocuteurs de top management, et à l’aise dans des contextes grands comptes. - Posture client first : disponible, réactif·ve, à l’écoute, capable de prioriser le client, d’intégrer les retours, d’anticiper les besoins et de gérer des situations sensibles. - Solides compétences en négociation et management : écoute active, questionnement, capacité à challenger, à gérer le conflit et à délivrer des feedbacks exigeants avec calme et clarté, dans une logique de progression collective. - Forte envie d’apprendre et de progresser, capable de challenger son équipe, de demander de l’aide et d’accepter d’être challengé.Pourquoi rejoindre Theodo ? L’environnement: 💼 Rejoindre un groupe de 750 personnes avec de nombreuses possibilités d’évolutions cross-entités 🤝 Chaque Theodoer est accompagné par un coach interne. Son objectif : t’épauler dans ton quotidien et parler objectifs de carrière via des séances de coaching hebdomadaires. 🎯 Participation à des projets associatifs grâce à la Fondation Theodo (Ada Tech School, Code Phoenix, Article 1…) 🎉 Soirées mensuelles, keynotes et week-end d’entreprise annuel Le package : 📈 Actionnariat salarié pour être associé à la réussite du groupe 💸 De l’épargne salariale avec un mécanisme d’intéressement en partenariat avec Epsor 🖥 Budget équipement (ordinateur, smartphone, écouteurs…) 🧒 Des avantages fournis par notre CSE (sport avec Gymlib,...) 🏖 5 semaines + 8 à 12 RTT/an 🩺 Mutuelle (SideCare) prise en charge à 50% 🍽 Carte ticket-restaurants Swile 🧒 Aides et places en crèche réservées Prêt à nous rejoindre ?
